Name: Mocktail System Handler Routes
Description: Defines the routing configuration for the Mocktail system handler.

Routes.Title: Access To General System UI Assets From The System Admin Controller Route
Routes.Description: Similar to the assets wildcard route defined below but this route specifically makes the system UI assets available to the AdminController and all constituent handler functions..

Routes.Title: Access To General System UI Assets From The System Mocking Controller Route
Routes.Description: Similar to the assets wildcard route defined below but this route specifically makes the system UI assets available to the MockingController and all constituent handler functions..

Routes.Title: General System UI, Static Wildcard Route
Routes.Description: The wildcard path for serving top-level system UI resources. This route will attempt to match any request starting with /ui/ and serve the corresponding static file from the .files/ui directory.

Routes.Title: General System UI Resources, Static Wildcard Route
Routes.Description: The wildcard path for serving assets such as CSS, JS, images etc for the system handler's UIs. This route will attempt to match any request starting with /assets/ and serve the corresponding static file from the .files/ui directory. This allows for easy referencing of static resources in the HTML files served by the system handler, ensuring that the necessary assets are available for the UI to function properly.Note: Where a wildcard Path is used (i.e /assets/*)  the FilePath MUST refer to the base internal directory that the files should be served from such that [BASE_DIR]/[Relative_Request_Path_Reveived_To_Handler] resolves to the file on disk, failure to set this path correctly will result in 404 Not Found errors being returned to the client.

Routes.Title: Authentication Check
Routes.Description: The /check-auth route handler, dynamically checks the authentication status of the user and forwards them to either /sign-in or /manage-ui based on their authentication status and account type. This allows for a seamless user experience by directing users to the appropriate interface based on their login status and permissions.

Routes.Title: Sign-In UI
Routes.Description: The /signin route handler, serves the sign-in.html file from the .files directory. this is the interface used by the user to log in or register.

Routes.Title: Sign-Up UI
Routes.Description: The /signup route handler, serves the sign-up.html file from the .files directory. this is the interface used by the user to create a new admin account.

Routes.Title: User Defined Endpoints Management via Sub-Handler
Routes.Description: The /usr/manage* route handler, delegates handling of any requests to paths starting with /usr/manage to the user-handler script located at ./res/handlers/usr/user-handler. This allows for modular handling of user-related routes and functionalities, keeping the root handler organized and focused on routing while the user-handler script can manage specific logic related to user operations.

The /api/status route handler, responds with a predefined JSON object indicating that the API is working. This can be used as a simple health check endpoint or for testing purposes to verify that the server is running and able to respond to requests.
